agent-registry.desc: Agent Registry is the unified inventory in Microsoft Agent 365 that lists every agent in an organization, so admins can find, quarantine or block them.

faq.a: Agent Registry is the unified inventory in Microsoft Agent 365 that lists every agent operating in an organization, including Microsoft and non-Microsoft agents.
faq.q: What is Agent Registry?

faq.a: Admins can use the inventory to find agents and to quarantine or block them.
faq.q: What can admins do with Agent Registry?

faq.a: Yes. The registry covers both Microsoft and non-Microsoft agents operating in the organization.
faq.q: Does Agent Registry include agents from outside Microsoft?

agent-registry.long:
Agent Registry is the unified inventory within Microsoft Agent 365 that lists every agent operating in an organization. It covers both Microsoft and non-Microsoft agents, giving administrators a single place to see which agents exist in their environment.

The registry is used for oversight and control. From the inventory, admins can find agents, quarantine them or block them. This makes it a central reference point for agent governance, particularly in organizations where agents come from several sources and are built or deployed by different teams. Documentation on how the registry converges with agent identity is available in the Microsoft Entra documentation on Agent ID.

On M365.FM, Agent Registry comes up in episodes that deal with agents, identity and governance. These include "Security Agent Fabric: Autonomous AI for Cyber Defense", "Graph-Powered AI Agents: An Enterprise Architecture Guide", "Microsoft Agent Builder — Simply Explained", "Codify Business Logic into a Digital Twin for AI Agents", "Secure Microsoft Copilot with Entra ID and Zero Trust" and "7-Step Microsoft 365 Sovereign Tenant Governance Framework".

ai-form-fill-assistance.desc: AI form fill assistance is a Copilot feature in Power Apps model-driven apps that suggests values for blank form fields and maps pasted content to fields.

faq.a: It is a Copilot feature in Power Apps model-driven apps that suggests values for blank form fields. Users can review the suggestions and accept them.
faq.q: What is AI form fill assistance?

faq.a: Smart paste reads pasted clipboard content, such as text or images, and maps it to fields on the form. The user then accepts the mapped values.
faq.q: What is smart paste in AI form fill assistance?

faq.a: It is described as a feature of Power Apps model-driven apps. Further availability details are in the official Microsoft documentation on form filling assistance.
faq.q: Which Power Apps apps support AI form fill assistance?

ai-form-fill-assistance.long:
AI form fill assistance is a Copilot feature in Power Apps model-driven apps. It suggests values for blank fields on a form, so that users do not have to type every entry by hand. The suggestions are offered to the user, who decides whether to accept them.

The feature includes a capability called smart paste. With smart paste, a user pastes clipboard content, such as text or an image, and the feature reads that content and maps it to the matching fields on the form. As with other suggestions, the user reviews the mapped values and accepts them before they are applied.

AI form fill assistance is used in situations where form data already exists in another place, such as copied text or an image, and needs to be entered into a model-driven app record. It sits within the broader set of Copilot capabilities in Power Apps, which belong to the Microsoft Power Platform.

The feature is documented by Microsoft in the Power Apps user documentation under form filling assistance. No M365.FM episodes are currently linked to this topic, and no related entities have been recorded.

al-language.desc: AL (Application Language) is Microsoft's programming language for Dynamics 365 Business Central, used to build extensions with tables, pages, codeunits and reports.
al-language.long:
AL (Application Language) is the programming language Microsoft provides for developing extensions to Dynamics 365 Business Central. It is used to describe the objects and logic that make up a Business Central extension, and development is usually done in Visual Studio Code.

With AL, developers define the building blocks of an extension: tables for data, pages for the user interface, codeunits for procedural logic, and reports for output and analysis. The language is also used to implement business rules, so that custom behavior can be added to Business Central without changing the base application directly.

AL is relevant for anyone searching for how Business Central is customized or extended, including developers, consultants and partners working in the Dynamics 365 ecosystem. It sits at the core of the extension-based development model of Dynamics 365 Business Central.

M365.FM covers topics across the Microsoft ecosystem, and AL (Application Language) is documented here as a product entity within that knowledge base. No specific episodes are currently linked to this entry.

altair-8800.desc: The Altair 8800 is a 1975 microcomputer from MITS, programmed through front-panel toggle switches and widely regarded as the first commercially successful personal computer.

faq.a: The Altair 8800 is a microcomputer released in 1975 by MITS. It was programmed using toggle switches on its front panel and is widely seen as the first commercially successful personal computer.
faq.q: What is the Altair 8800?

faq.a: The Altair 8800 was made by MITS and released in 1975.
faq.q: Who made the Altair 8800?

faq.a: It is referenced in the episode "Mainframe Architecture Lessons for Azure Cloud Design", published on 2025-11-03.
faq.q: Where does the Altair 8800 appear on M365.FM?

altair-8800.long:
The Altair 8800 is a microcomputer released in 1975 by MITS. It was programmed through toggle switches on its front panel, and it is widely seen as the first commercially successful personal computer.

As a product, the Altair 8800 belongs to the early history of personal computing, a period before graphical interfaces and packaged business software. Its front-panel switch programming is a defining feature and a useful reference point when comparing early hardware with later systems. The facts available here do not cover its technical specifications, pricing or software ecosystem, so this page does not go into those details.

On M365.FM, the Altair 8800 appears in connection with the episode "Mainframe Architecture Lessons for Azure Cloud Design" (published 2025-11-03). That episode places historical computing platforms alongside cloud architecture, using earlier system designs as context for how Azure environments are planned. The Altair 8800 serves there as a historical reference rather than as a current Microsoft product.

amazon-bedrock.desc: Amazon Bedrock is an AWS service for building generative AI applications and agents on foundation models, covered on M365.FM in the context of Microsoft AI.

faq.a: Amazon Bedrock is an AWS service for building generative AI applications and agents on foundation models.
faq.q: What is Amazon Bedrock?

faq.a: It is referenced in episodes about Microsoft's AI platform, such as "Build Auditable AI Agents with Azure AI Foundry" and "Microsoft AI Gateway - Simply Explained", where it serves as a point of comparison with the AI offerings of another cloud provider.
faq.q: Why does Amazon Bedrock appear on M365.FM?

amazon-bedrock.long:
Amazon Bedrock is a service from AWS (Amazon Web Services) for building generative AI applications and agents on foundation models. It is used by teams that want to create AI-based applications and agent-style solutions on top of existing foundation models rather than training models from scratch.

On M365.FM, Amazon Bedrock is not the main subject of any episode but appears as a point of reference in discussions of Microsoft's AI platform and architecture. It is mentioned in connection with the episodes "Build Auditable AI Agents with Azure AI Foundry", "Microsoft AI Gateway - Simply Explained", "Azure Local - Simply Explained", "Security Agent Fabric: Autonomous AI for Cyber Defense" and "How Microsoft Built an Enterprise AI Architecture Advantage". These episodes deal with agents, AI governance, hybrid infrastructure, security and enterprise AI design in the Microsoft ecosystem, where comparisons with other cloud providers' AI offerings can be relevant.

The available information does not specify product features, model catalogs, pricing or regional availability, so these are not described here. For details on Amazon Bedrock itself, the official AWS documentation is the authoritative source.

amazon-s3.desc: Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) is an Amazon Web Services object storage service that holds data as objects in buckets and can be referenced from Microsoft Fabric via OneLake shortcuts.

faq.a: Amazon S3 (Amazon Simple Storage Service) is an object storage service from Amazon Web Services. It stores data as objects in buckets.
faq.q: What is Amazon S3?

faq.a: Microsoft Fabric can reference data in Amazon S3 through OneLake shortcuts. This allows S3-hosted data to be used from within the Fabric and OneLake environment.
faq.q: How does Amazon S3 relate to Microsoft Fabric?

faq.a: It is mentioned in episodes such as "Eliminate Data Silos with Microsoft Fabric and OneLake" and "DP-600 Training 2/4: Fabric Dataflows, Pipelines & Notebooks", among others.
faq.q: Where does Amazon S3 appear on M365.FM?

amazon-s3.long:
Amazon S3, short for Amazon Simple Storage Service, is an object storage service from Amazon Web Services. It stores data as objects that are organized in buckets. Because it sits outside the Microsoft cloud, it is often discussed in Microsoft-centered scenarios as an example of data that lives in another platform.

In the Microsoft ecosystem, Amazon S3 is relevant mainly through Microsoft Fabric. Fabric can reference S3 data through OneLake shortcuts, which makes it possible to work with data stored in S3 buckets without treating it as a separate silo. This connects the service to the wider topic of unifying data across clouds and storage locations in OneLake.

On M365.FM, Amazon S3 comes up in several episodes. These include "DP-600 Training 2/4: Fabric Dataflows, Pipelines & Notebooks", "Eliminate Data Silos with Microsoft Fabric and OneLake", "Microsoft Graph Connectors - Simply Explained" and "Archive Inactive SharePoint Sites with Azure Blob Storage". In these discussions it appears as a point of comparison or integration alongside Microsoft-native storage and data services such as OneLake and Azure Blob Storage.

apache-kafka.desc: Apache Kafka is an open-source distributed event streaming platform from the Apache Software Foundation for high-throughput event streams, data pipelines and analytics.

faq.a: Apache Kafka is an open-source distributed event streaming platform from the Apache Software Foundation. It is used for high-throughput event streams, data pipelines and analytics.
faq.q: What is Apache Kafka?

faq.a: Yes. Replaying past events is one of its described capabilities, which allows historical event data to be reprocessed.
faq.q: Can Apache Kafka replay past events?

faq.a: It is referenced in the episodes "Azure Event Hubs - Simply Explained", "Microsoft Graph API Discovery for Enterprise Semantic Search" and "Upgrade Java 8 Apps to Java 21 with AI Agents".
faq.q: Where does Apache Kafka appear on M365.FM?

apache-kafka.long:
Apache Kafka is an open-source distributed event streaming platform developed under the Apache Software Foundation. It is used to handle high-throughput streams of events, to build data pipelines and to feed analytics workloads. A defining characteristic is the ability to replay past events, so consumers can reprocess historical data rather than only reading the most recent messages.

In practice, Apache Kafka serves as a backbone for moving event data between systems. Producers publish events, and separate consumers read them independently, which allows the same stream to support several downstream uses such as real-time processing and analytical reporting.

On M365.FM, Apache Kafka comes up in the context of Microsoft and Azure topics. The episode "Azure Event Hubs - Simply Explained" (2026-07-15) is relevant for anyone comparing event streaming approaches on Azure. It also appears in discussions around "Microsoft Graph API Discovery for Enterprise Semantic Search" (2026-05-28) and "Upgrade Java 8 Apps to Java 21 with AI Agents" (2025-11-28), where event streaming and Java-based applications are part of the wider technical setting.

apache-spark.desc: Apache Spark is an open-source distributed processing engine that splits large data workloads across many machines, originally developed at UC Berkeley.

faq.a: Apache Spark is an open-source distributed processing engine that splits large data workloads across many machines. It began at UC Berkeley and is maintained by the Apache Software Foundation.
faq.q: What is Apache Spark?

faq.a: Apache Spark is maintained by the Apache Software Foundation. The project originated at UC Berkeley.
faq.q: Who maintains Apache Spark?

faq.a: It is mentioned in episodes about Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databricks, such as "Microsoft Fabric - Simply Explained" and "Azure Databricks - Simply Explained", as well as "Train AI Models with Microsoft Fabric Notebooks".
faq.q: Where does Apache Spark appear on M365.FM?

apache-spark.long:
Apache Spark is an open-source distributed processing engine that splits large data workloads across many machines. The project began at UC Berkeley and is maintained by the Apache Software Foundation.

Spark is used when a dataset or computation is too large for a single machine. By dividing the work across a cluster, it allows data processing tasks to run in parallel. On M365.FM, the term appears in the context of data and analytics platforms in the Microsoft ecosystem, where distributed processing underpins large-scale data preparation and model training.

On M365.FM, Apache Spark is mentioned in episodes covering Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databricks. These include "Train AI Models with Microsoft Fabric Notebooks", "Microsoft Fabric - Simply Explained", "Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse Governance and Data Lineage", "Secure Microsoft Fabric Data Pipelines" and "Azure Databricks - Simply Explained". It also comes up in the episode "Speed Power BI with OneLake and Direct Lake".

Listeners looking for background on how Spark fits alongside Fabric, Databricks, lakehouse concepts and Power BI can use these episodes as entry points.

api-management-developer-portal.desc: The API Management developer portal is a customizable website within an Azure API Management instance where API consumers discover APIs, read documentation and obtain subscription keys.

faq.a: It is a customizable website that is part of an Azure API Management instance. API consumers use it to discover APIs, read documentation, obtain subscription keys and try API calls in the browser.
faq.q: What is the API Management developer portal?

faq.a: It is aimed at API consumers, meaning developers who want to find and use the APIs published through an Azure API Management instance.
faq.q: Who uses the API Management developer portal?

faq.a: Yes. It is described as a customizable website, and Microsoft provides documentation on how to work with it.
faq.q: Can the API Management developer portal be customized?

api-management-developer-portal.long:
The API Management developer portal is a customizable website that is part of an Azure API Management instance. It serves as the consumer-facing side of the service: a place where developers who want to use an organization's APIs can find them and learn how they work.

According to its description, API consumers use the portal to discover available APIs, read their documentation, obtain subscription keys and try API calls directly in the browser. This makes it a self-service entry point for onboarding external or internal developers, while API publishers manage the underlying APIs in Azure API Management itself. Because the portal is customizable, its content and appearance can be adapted by the team operating the instance.

Microsoft documents the portal in its Azure API Management documentation, including a guide on how to work with and customize it.

On M365.FM, the API Management developer portal appears in connection with the episode "Secure Azure Networking with Rex de Koning [MVP-MCT]", published on 2026-07-07.

api-plugins.desc: API plugins for Microsoft 365 Copilot let Copilot call a live external API at runtime to perform actions such as creating a ticket, without indexing data into Microsoft 365.

faq.a: They are an extensibility model in which Copilot calls a live external API at runtime. They are typically used to perform actions such as creating a ticket or updating a record.
faq.q: What are API plugins for Microsoft 365 Copilot?

faq.a: No. With API plugins, the data is not indexed into Microsoft 365; Copilot calls the external API live when needed.
faq.q: Is data from the external system indexed into Microsoft 365?

faq.a: It is discussed in the episode "Build Custom Microsoft 365 Copilot Plugins", published on 2025-08-14.
faq.q: Where is this topic covered on M365.FM?

api-plugins.long:
API plugins for Microsoft 365 Copilot are an extensibility model in which Copilot calls a live external API at runtime. They are typically used to perform actions, for example creating a ticket or updating a record in another system.

A defining characteristic of this model is that the data is not indexed into Microsoft 365. Instead of copying external content into Microsoft 365 ahead of time, Copilot reaches out to the external API when a request requires it. This distinguishes API plugins from approaches that bring external content into Microsoft 365 for later retrieval.

On M365.FM, the topic appears in the episode "Build Custom Microsoft 365 Copilot Plugins" (published 2025-08-14), which covers building custom plugins for Microsoft 365 Copilot. Microsoft provides an official overview of plugins in its Learn documentation, which is the reference for technical details on how the extensibility model works.

application-insights.desc: Application Insights is the application performance monitoring feature of Azure Monitor, tracking request rates, response times, exceptions and dependency calls of applications.

faq.a: Application Insights is the application performance monitoring feature of Azure Monitor. It tracks request rates, response times, exceptions and dependency calls of applications.
faq.q: What is Application Insights?

faq.a: Application Insights is a feature of Azure Monitor. It provides the application-level performance telemetry within the wider Azure Monitor monitoring capabilities.
faq.q: How does Application Insights relate to Azure Monitor?

faq.a: It is discussed in episodes such as "Azure Monitor — Simply Explained", "Azure Functions - Simply Explained", "Build Self-Healing Automation with Telemetry and Observability" and "Monitor Business Central Telemetry with Power BI".
faq.q: Where does Application Insights appear on M365.FM?

application-insights.long:
Application Insights is the application performance monitoring feature of Azure Monitor. It collects telemetry from running applications, including request rates, response times, exceptions and dependency calls. This data helps teams understand how an application behaves in production and where problems occur.

Because it is part of Azure Monitor, Application Insights fits into the broader observability tooling of the Azure platform. Typical uses include checking how quickly an application responds to requests, finding exceptions that users encounter, and tracing calls from an application to the services it depends on.

On M365.FM, Application Insights appears in several episodes that touch on monitoring and telemetry. These include "Azure Monitor — Simply Explained" and "Azure Functions - Simply Explained", as well as "Build Microsoft Copilot Plugins with Azure Functions" and "Deploy Web Apps to Azure App Service Without Boilerplate". It is also covered in the context of operational feedback loops in "Build Self-Healing Automation with Telemetry and Observability" and in "Monitor Business Central Telemetry with Power BI".

argo-cd.desc: Argo CD is an open-source, CNCF graduated GitOps continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes that compares live cluster state with Git and shows sync status and health.

faq.a: Argo CD is an open-source, CNCF graduated GitOps continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes. It compares the live cluster state with the state defined in Git.
faq.q: What is Argo CD?

faq.a: The web UI offers views of sync status, health and history for the applications it manages.
faq.q: What does the Argo CD web UI show?

faq.a: It is mentioned in the episodes "GitOps - Simply Explained", "Scaling CI-CD: The Governance Blueprint" and "Platform Engineering: The New Operating Model for Azure".
faq.q: Where does Argo CD appear on M365.FM?

argo-cd.long:
Argo CD is an open-source GitOps continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes. It is a graduated project of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF). Its core function is to compare the live state of a Kubernetes cluster with the desired state stored in Git, so that differences between the two can be identified.

Argo CD provides a web UI where teams can view sync status, application health and deployment history. This makes it a common reference point when explaining the GitOps model, in which Git acts as the source of truth for what should run in a cluster and the cluster is continuously checked against it.

On M365.FM, Argo CD appears in episodes that cover delivery and operating models in the Microsoft and Azure ecosystem. These include "GitOps - Simply Explained", which introduces the GitOps approach, "Scaling CI-CD: The Governance Blueprint", which looks at governing continuous integration and delivery at scale, and "Platform Engineering: The New Operating Model for Azure", which discusses platform engineering as an operating model for Azure.

This page does not list specific versions, features beyond those described above, or configuration details. For installation and usage instructions, the project's own documentation is the authoritative source.

attack-simulation-training.desc: Attack simulation training is a Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 feature that sends simulated phishing to users and assigns follow-up training based on their behaviour.

faq.a: It is a Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 feature that sends realistic simulated phishing to users and assigns follow-up training based on their behaviour.
faq.q: What is attack simulation training?

faq.a: Attack simulation training is part of Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2.
faq.q: Which Microsoft product includes attack simulation training?

faq.a: Training is assigned based on how users behave when they receive the simulated phishing messages.
faq.q: How is follow-up training assigned?

attack-simulation-training.long:
Attack simulation training is a feature of Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2. It sends realistic simulated phishing messages to users in an organization and then assigns follow-up training depending on how those users respond.

The feature is used to test how people react to phishing attempts in a controlled setting and to turn the results into targeted training. Because the follow-up is based on observed behaviour, training is directed at the users who interacted with a simulated message rather than applied uniformly.

Attack simulation training sits within the Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 offering, which means it is tied to that licensing tier rather than being a standalone product. Organizations evaluating the feature therefore need to consider it as part of the broader Defender for Office 365 capabilities.

On M365.FM, the feature is covered in the episode "Microsoft Defender for Office 365 - Simply Explained" (2026-07-22), which discusses Microsoft Defender for Office 365 and the role attack simulation training plays within it.

auto-capture.desc: Auto capture in Dynamics 365 Sales finds emails and meetings tied to customer records and suggests them to the seller for review and tracking in the CRM.

faq.a: Auto capture is a Dynamics 365 Sales feature that finds emails and meetings related to customer records and suggests them to the seller. The seller reviews the suggestions and tracks them in the CRM.
faq.q: What is Auto capture in Dynamics 365 Sales?

faq.a: According to the available description, Auto capture suggests emails and meetings to the seller for review and tracking. The review step remains with the seller.
faq.q: Does Auto capture track items automatically without review?

faq.a: It appears in the episode "Dynamics 365 Sales Insights - Simply Explained", dated 2026-08-17.
faq.q: Where is Auto capture discussed on M365.FM?

auto-capture.long:
Auto capture is a feature of Dynamics 365 Sales. It identifies emails and meetings that relate to customer records and suggests them to the seller, who can then review them and track them in the CRM. The name is also written as Auto-capture or Auto Capture.

The feature is used to reduce the manual effort of keeping customer communication up to date in the CRM. Instead of a seller searching their mailbox and calendar for relevant items, Auto capture surfaces likely matches against customer records. The seller stays in control by reviewing the suggestions before an item is tracked.

On M365.FM, Auto capture is covered in the episode "Dynamics 365 Sales Insights - Simply Explained" (2026-08-17), which discusses it in the context of Dynamics 365 Sales Insights. No further configuration details, licensing information or version specifics are included in the available facts, so this page limits itself to the core behavior described above.

autogen.desc: AutoGen is a product covered on M365.FM in episodes about AI agents, Microsoft Foundry, Copilot Studio, Semantic Kernel and enterprise agent architecture.

faq.a: AutoGen is a product listed in the M365.FM knowledge base. It is tied to the site's coverage of AI agents, though no official description is stored here.
faq.q: What is AutoGen?

faq.a: It is linked to six episodes, including those on graph-powered AI agents, production AI agents with Microsoft Foundry, scaling Copilot Studio, and secure IT ops agents with MCP and Semantic Kernel.
faq.q: Where does AutoGen appear on M365.FM?

faq.a: The linked episodes cover enterprise agent architecture, Microsoft Foundry, Copilot Studio, Semantic Kernel, MCP, and security and shadow IT in Microsoft 365.
faq.q: Which topics are discussed alongside AutoGen?

autogen.long:
AutoGen is a product that appears in M365.FM's coverage of AI agents in the Microsoft ecosystem. The knowledge base holds no official description, documentation link or product page for it, so this entry is limited to where the topic is discussed.

On M365.FM, AutoGen is connected to episodes about building and operating agent-based solutions. These include a guide to graph-powered AI agents and enterprise architecture, a conversation on how AI has changed software development and the move toward agentic systems, and a session on scaling Copilot Studio. It is also linked to an episode on production AI agents with Microsoft Foundry, an episode on secure AI agents and shadow IT in Microsoft 365, and an episode on building secure IT operations agents with MCP and Semantic Kernel.

Taken together, the episodes place AutoGen in the context of agent design, production deployment, security and governance, and developer tooling around the Microsoft platform. Listeners searching for AutoGen can use these episodes to see how the topic relates to Microsoft Foundry, Copilot Studio, Semantic Kernel and MCP. The episodes themselves are the authoritative source for how AutoGen is positioned in each discussion.

aws-direct-connect.desc: AWS Direct Connect is an Amazon Web Services offering that provides a dedicated private network connection from on-premises or colocation facilities to AWS.

faq.a: AWS Direct Connect is an Amazon Web Services offering that provides a dedicated private network connection from on-premises or colocation facilities to AWS.
faq.q: What is AWS Direct Connect?

faq.a: No. It is described as a connection that does not traverse the public internet, linking on-premises or colocation facilities directly to AWS.
faq.q: Does AWS Direct Connect use the public internet?

faq.a: This entry does not include those details. They are available in the official AWS documentation.
faq.q: Where can details such as pricing or supported capacities be found?

aws-direct-connect.long:
AWS Direct Connect is an Amazon Web Services offering that provides a dedicated private network connection from on-premises or colocation facilities to AWS without traversing the public internet.

In practice, organizations use a dedicated connection of this kind to link their own data centers or colocation environments directly to AWS. Because traffic does not travel over the public internet, the connection is described as private. This type of setup is typically considered when a hybrid architecture requires a defined network path between local infrastructure and cloud resources.

On M365.FM, AWS Direct Connect is catalogued as a product entity within the broader coverage of the Microsoft ecosystem and neighboring cloud platforms. No related topics or episodes are currently linked to this entry, and no further technical details are recorded here beyond the definition above. For specifications, supported capacities, locations and pricing, the official AWS documentation is the authoritative source.

aws-iam.desc: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls access to AWS resources through users, roles and policies, with IAM Identity Center adding single sign-on and MFA.

faq.a: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is a product that controls access to AWS resources through users, roles and policies.
faq.q: What is AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)?

faq.a: IAM Identity Center adds single sign-on and multi-factor authentication (MFA) across AWS accounts.
faq.q: What does IAM Identity Center add?

faq.a: It is covered in the episode "AWS vs Microsoft Entra for Enterprise Cloud Identity" from February 26, 2026.
faq.q: Where does AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) appear on M365.FM?

aws-iam.long:
AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is a product that controls access to AWS resources. It does this through users, roles and policies, which together define who or what can interact with resources in an AWS environment and under which conditions.

IAM Identity Center extends this model by adding single sign-on and multi-factor authentication (MFA) across AWS accounts. This allows sign-in and authentication requirements to be handled centrally rather than account by account.

On M365.FM, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) appears in the episode "AWS vs Microsoft Entra for Enterprise Cloud Identity" (February 26, 2026), which places AWS identity services alongside Microsoft Entra in the context of enterprise cloud identity. The comparison is relevant for organizations that operate in both the Microsoft and AWS ecosystems and need to understand how identity and access control are handled on each side.

azure-ad-b2c.desc: Azure AD B2C is Microsoft's earlier customer identity service for consumer-facing apps, configured with user flows or custom policies and succeeded by Microsoft Entra External ID.

faq.a: Azure AD B2C is Microsoft's earlier customer identity service for consumer-facing apps. It manages identity for external users and is configured using user flows or XML-based custom policies.
faq.q: What is Azure AD B2C?

faq.a: It is configured with user flows or with XML-based custom policies. User flows address common scenarios, while custom policies offer more detailed control through XML.
faq.q: How is Azure AD B2C configured?

faq.a: Azure AD B2C has been succeeded by Microsoft Entra External ID, which is Microsoft's current offering for external identity scenarios.
faq.q: What replaced Azure AD B2C?

azure-ad-b2c.long:
Azure AD B2C (Azure Active Directory B2C) is a Microsoft customer identity service designed for consumer-facing applications. It handles sign-up and sign-in for an app's external users, such as customers, rather than for an organization's own employees.

The service is configured in two ways: with user flows, and with XML-based custom policies. User flows cover standard identity scenarios, while custom policies allow more detailed control over the authentication journey through XML configuration.

Azure AD B2C is described as Microsoft's earlier customer identity offering. It has been succeeded by Microsoft Entra External ID, which is now the product to consider for external identity scenarios. Information about Azure AD B2C therefore appears mainly in the context of existing deployments and of understanding how the newer service relates to the older one.

On M365.FM, the topic comes up in episodes covering external identity and customer-facing solutions, including "Microsoft Entra External ID for Digital Trust and Growth" and "Microsoft Entra as a Complete IAM Platform". It also appears in discussions of customer portals and multi-tenant applications built on Power Pages and Dataverse, such as "Build Customer Portals with Power Pages and Dataverse" and "Building Multi-Tenant SaaS with Power Pages and Dataverse".

azure-ad-graph.desc: Azure AD Graph is the legacy Microsoft directory API that Microsoft deprecated and retired in favor of Microsoft Graph, and it did not offer API-level activity logging.

faq.a: Azure AD Graph is a legacy Microsoft directory API. Microsoft deprecated and retired it in favor of Microsoft Graph.
faq.q: What is Azure AD Graph?

faq.a: Microsoft Graph replaced Azure AD Graph as the API for working with Microsoft 365 and directory data.
faq.q: What replaced Azure AD Graph?

faq.a: No. Azure AD Graph did not provide API-level activity logging.
faq.q: Did Azure AD Graph provide activity logging?

azure-ad-graph.long:
Azure AD Graph is a legacy Microsoft directory API. Microsoft deprecated it and retired it in favor of Microsoft Graph, which is now the API used to work with Microsoft 365 and directory data. One documented limitation of Azure AD Graph is that it did not provide API-level activity logging.

Because Azure AD Graph has been retired, it is mainly relevant today in migration and modernization work. Scripts, applications and automation that once called the older directory API need to be moved to Microsoft Graph. The lack of API-level activity logging is also a point of comparison when discussing auditing and visibility of API calls in directory-related automation.

On M365.FM, Azure AD Graph comes up in episodes that deal with Microsoft Graph and related migration and security topics. These include "Migrate Exchange Web Services to Microsoft Graph with Glen Scales [MVP]", "Microsoft Graph Automation Architecture: Beyond Scripts", "Service Principal Security: Stop Using Personal Accounts" and "How Microsoft Graph Connects Microsoft 365 Data and Context". In these discussions the legacy API serves as the background against which Microsoft Graph, service principal-based automation and architectural approaches to Microsoft 365 data are explained.

azure-advisor.desc: Azure Advisor is a free, built-in Azure service that analyzes resource configuration and usage and gives personalized recommendations across five pillars.

faq.a: Azure Advisor is a free, built-in Azure service that analyzes resource configuration and usage and provides personalized recommendations. These cover cost, security, reliability, performance and operational excellence.
faq.q: What is Azure Advisor?

faq.a: Recommendations fall into five categories: cost, security, reliability, performance and operational excellence.
faq.q: Which areas do Azure Advisor recommendations cover?

faq.a: No. Azure Advisor is described as a free service that is built into Azure.
faq.q: Is Azure Advisor a paid service?

azure-advisor.long:
Azure Advisor is a free, built-in Azure service that analyzes the configuration and usage of Azure resources and returns personalized recommendations. The recommendations are grouped into five areas: cost, security, reliability, performance and operational excellence.

The service is used to review an existing Azure environment and identify where changes could reduce spending, close security gaps, improve resilience or raise performance. Because it draws on how resources are actually configured and used, its guidance is specific to the environment being examined rather than generic. Official documentation is available on Microsoft Learn.

Azure Advisor appears on M365.FM in several episodes. The episode "Azure Advisor - Simply Explained" (2026-07-19) covers the service directly. It also connects to cost topics in "Azure Cost Management - Simply Explained" (2026-07-19) and "Stop Azure Cost Entropy with Ownership and Budget Controls" (2026-01-17), to reliability in "Design Reliable and Resilient Azure Architectures" (2025-11-03), and to governance in "Azure Policy - Simply Explained" (2026-07-15). Another related episode is "How to Build Low-Cost AI Agents in Microsoft Cloud" (2026-06-10).

azure-ai-content-understanding.desc: Azure AI Content Understanding is a Microsoft AI service that turns documents, images and other content into structured results based on fields defined in a schema.

faq.a: It is a Microsoft AI service that takes documents, images and other content and returns structured results based on fields defined in a schema.
faq.q: What is Azure AI Content Understanding?

faq.a: The schema defines the fields the service should return, so the extracted information can be used by business processes.
faq.q: What is the schema used for in Azure AI Content Understanding?

faq.a: It appears in the episode "Copilot Studio AI Agents and RAG with Nilüfer Doğan [MVP]", dated 2026-06-27.
faq.q: Where does Azure AI Content Understanding appear on M365.FM?

azure-ai-content-understanding.long:
Azure AI Content Understanding is a Microsoft AI service that processes documents, images and other content and returns structured results. The output is shaped by fields defined in a schema, which allows the extracted information to be used directly in business processes.

The core idea described for the service is the schema-driven approach: instead of receiving unstructured text or loosely formatted output, the caller specifies which fields are expected, and the service returns values for those fields. This makes the extracted data easier to hand over to downstream steps such as workflows, records or reporting.

On M365.FM, Azure AI Content Understanding appears in the episode "Copilot Studio AI Agents and RAG with Nilüfer Doğan [MVP]", published on 2026-06-27. The episode connects to topics such as AI agents and retrieval-augmented generation, where structured information drawn from documents and other content can be relevant.

No further details, such as supported content types, pricing, availability or version information, are included in the source facts for this page, so they are not described here.

azure-ai-document-intelligence.desc: Azure AI Document Intelligence, formerly Azure Form Recognizer, is a cloud AI service that extracts text, key-value pairs, tables and structure from documents.

faq.a: Azure AI Document Intelligence is a cloud AI service that extracts text, key-value pairs, tables and structure from documents. It provides prebuilt and custom models and is accessed through REST APIs and SDKs.
faq.q: What is Azure AI Document Intelligence?

faq.a: It was formerly named Azure Form Recognizer.
faq.q: What was Azure AI Document Intelligence called before?

faq.a: Developers call the service through REST APIs and SDKs, using either prebuilt models or custom models to extract structured data from documents.
faq.q: How do developers use Azure AI Document Intelligence?

azure-ai-document-intelligence.long:
Azure AI Document Intelligence is a cloud AI service from Microsoft for extracting information from documents. It was previously known as Azure Form Recognizer. The service reads documents and returns text, key-value pairs, tables and document structure as structured output.

The service offers prebuilt models as well as custom models. Prebuilt models cover common document extraction scenarios without additional training, while custom models allow the extraction to be adapted to specific document types. Developers access the service through REST APIs and SDKs, which makes it possible to integrate document processing into applications and workflows.

Typical uses include turning scanned or digital documents into structured data that other systems can process, for example by pulling field values and table contents out of forms. Official technical documentation is published on Microsoft Learn.

This page is a reference entry on M365.FM. No episodes or related topics are currently linked to Azure AI Document Intelligence in the knowledge base.

azure-ai-services.desc: Azure AI services is Microsoft's family of prebuilt AI APIs on Azure, formerly Azure Cognitive Services, covering vision, speech, language and decision capabilities.

faq.a: Azure AI services is Microsoft's family of prebuilt AI APIs on Azure. It covers vision, speech, language and decision capabilities that apps and flows can call.
faq.q: What is Azure AI services?

faq.a: Azure AI services was formerly named Azure Cognitive Services.
faq.q: What was Azure AI services previously called?

faq.a: It is referenced in episodes such as "Azure AI Infrastructure Architecture for C-Level Leaders", "Fix Common Azure AI Foundry Project Failures" and "Build Production AI Apps with Azure OpenAI and Power Platform".
faq.q: Where is Azure AI services discussed on M365.FM?

azure-ai-services.long:
Azure AI services is a Microsoft family of prebuilt AI APIs on Azure. It was formerly known as Azure Cognitive Services. The services cover vision, speech, language and decision capabilities, and they are designed to be called by applications and automated flows rather than built from scratch.

In practice, Azure AI services is used when a solution needs ready-made AI functions, such as analyzing images, processing spoken audio, working with text or supporting decisions, without training a custom model first. Because the capabilities are exposed as APIs, they can be integrated into custom apps and into workflow tools that call external services.

On M365.FM, Azure AI services appears in several episodes that place it within wider Azure and Microsoft AI scenarios. These include "Azure AI Infrastructure Architecture for C-Level Leaders", "Fix Common Azure AI Foundry Project Failures" and "Build Production AI Apps with Azure OpenAI and Power Platform". It also comes up in discussions touching Azure AI Foundry and agentic AI, such as "Beyond Copilot: Building AI That Works in the Real World with Azure AI Foundry and Agentic AI for Frontline Workers with Fergus Kidd [MVP]", and in "Copilot Studio AI Agents and RAG with Nilüfer Doğan [MVP]". Networking and security topics are covered in "Azure Private Link - Simply Explained".

azure-api-center.desc: Azure API Center is an Azure service that builds a central inventory of an organization's APIs and MCP servers for registration, description, governance and discovery.

faq.a: Azure API Center is an Azure service that provides a central inventory of an organization's APIs and MCP servers. It lets them be registered, described, governed and discovered for reuse.
faq.q: What is Azure API Center?

faq.a: According to its description, the service covers an organization's APIs and MCP servers. Both can be kept in the same central inventory.
faq.q: What kinds of assets can be listed in Azure API Center?

faq.a: It is associated with the episode "Azure MCP Server - Simply Explained", published on 15 July 2026.
faq.q: Where does Azure API Center appear on M365.FM?

azure-api-center.long:
Azure API Center is an Azure service for building a central inventory of an organization's APIs and MCP servers. Its purpose is to give teams one place where these assets can be registered, described, governed and discovered, so that they can be found and reused instead of being rebuilt or tracked in separate lists.

In practice, an inventory of this kind addresses a common organizational problem: APIs and MCP servers are often spread across teams and environments, and it is unclear what exists, who owns it and how it is documented. By registering these assets centrally and attaching descriptions to them, Azure API Center supports governance of the API landscape and makes reuse easier for developers looking for existing capabilities.

The inclusion of MCP servers alongside APIs reflects the growing role of the Model Context Protocol in the Microsoft ecosystem, where servers expose tools and data to AI-based applications. Treating them as part of the same inventory allows them to be managed with the same approach of registration, description and discovery.

On M365.FM, Azure API Center appears in the context of the episode "Azure MCP Server - Simply Explained" (published 15 July 2026), which covers the Azure MCP Server topic.

azure-api-management.desc: Azure API Management (APIM) is a Microsoft Azure service for publishing, securing, throttling and monitoring APIs, related to Azure Functions and Azure Logic Apps.

azure-app-configuration.desc: Azure App Configuration is a managed Azure service that centralizes application settings and feature flags as key-value pairs, shared and updated across multiple applications.

faq.a: Azure App Configuration is a managed Azure service that centralizes application settings and feature flags as key-value pairs. Multiple applications can share and update this configuration.
faq.q: What is Azure App Configuration?

faq.a: It stores application settings and feature flags in the form of key-value pairs. Keeping them in one managed service lets several applications use the same configuration.
faq.q: What does Azure App Configuration store?

faq.a: It is mentioned in the episode "Build Fusion Apps with Power Apps and Azure Functions" from 2025-08-11.
faq.q: Where does Azure App Configuration appear on M365.FM?

azure-app-configuration.long:
Azure App Configuration is a managed service in Microsoft Azure that centralizes application settings and feature flags. Configuration is stored as key-value pairs, which allows multiple applications to read from the same source instead of each keeping its own copy of settings.

The service is used to share configuration across applications and to update it in one place. Because settings and feature flags are held centrally, changes can be made to the stored values without maintaining separate configuration for every application that depends on them. Details on capabilities, supported scenarios and setup are described in the official Microsoft Learn documentation for the service.

On M365.FM, Azure App Configuration appears in the episode "Build Fusion Apps with Power Apps and Azure Functions" (published 2025-08-11), which places it in the context of building applications that combine Power Apps with Azure Functions.

azure-application-gateway.desc: Azure Application Gateway is a Layer 7 web traffic load balancer in Azure that understands HTTP and HTTPS, routes requests by web rules and can terminate TLS.

faq.a: Azure Application Gateway is a Layer 7 web traffic load balancer in Azure. It understands HTTP and HTTPS and routes requests to back-end servers based on web rules.
faq.q: What is Azure Application Gateway?

faq.a: Yes. According to its description, Azure Application Gateway can handle TLS termination before traffic reaches the back-end servers.
faq.q: Can Azure Application Gateway terminate TLS?

faq.a: M365.FM also has "Simply Explained" episodes on Azure Load Balancer, Azure Traffic Manager, Azure API Management and Azure Front Door, which cover related traffic and delivery services.
faq.q: Which other Azure services are covered alongside Azure Application Gateway on M365.FM?

azure-application-gateway.long:
Azure Application Gateway is a Layer 7 web traffic load balancer in Azure. Because it operates at the application layer, it understands HTTP and HTTPS traffic and can make routing decisions based on web rules rather than only on network-level information.

In practice, Azure Application Gateway sits in front of back-end servers and directs incoming web requests according to the rules that have been configured. It can also handle TLS termination, meaning encrypted connections are ended at the gateway before the traffic is passed on to the back-end servers. These capabilities make it a typical building block for web applications hosted in Azure that need request-aware routing.

Azure Application Gateway is often discussed alongside other Azure traffic and delivery services, including Azure Load Balancer, Azure Traffic Manager, Azure Front Door and Azure API Management. Comparing them helps clarify which service operates at which layer and for which kind of traffic.

On M365.FM, Azure Application Gateway appears in several episodes: "Run Azure Application Gateway Without Public IP Exposure", "Azure Application Gateway - Simply Explained", and the related "Simply Explained" episodes on Azure Load Balancer, Azure Traffic Manager, Azure API Management and Azure Front Door. Official documentation is available on Microsoft Learn.

azure-arc.desc: Azure Arc is a Microsoft service that connects servers and Kubernetes clusters running outside Azure, such as on-premises or at the edge, to Azure management.

faq.a: Azure Arc is a Microsoft service that connects servers and Kubernetes clusters running outside Azure, for example on-premises or at the edge, to Azure management.
faq.q: What is Azure Arc?

faq.a: According to the available description, Azure Arc connects servers and Kubernetes clusters that run outside Azure, such as in on-premises or edge environments.
faq.q: What kinds of resources can Azure Arc connect?

faq.a: It is covered in episodes such as "Azure Arc - Simply Explained" and "Cut Cloud Costs with Azure Arc and Azure Local on Mini PCs", and it also comes up in hybrid cloud and Azure management discussions.
faq.q: Where is Azure Arc covered on M365.FM?

azure-arc.long:
Azure Arc is a Microsoft service that connects servers and Kubernetes clusters running outside Azure to Azure management. These resources can sit on-premises, at the edge, or in other environments, and Azure Arc brings them under a common management approach alongside resources that run in Azure itself. Microsoft documents the service in its Azure Arc overview on Microsoft Learn.

The service is relevant for hybrid scenarios, where organizations operate infrastructure in several locations but want consistent oversight through Azure. Within M365.FM, Azure Arc is discussed in connection with hybrid cloud topics such as Azure Local and landing zones, as well as with Azure management services like Azure Update Manager and Azure Resource Manager.

Azure Arc appears in several M365.FM episodes. "Azure Arc - Simply Explained" gives an introduction to the service. "Cut Cloud Costs with Azure Arc and Azure Local on Mini PCs" covers it in a cost-focused hybrid context, and "Azure Local and Landing Zones: How to Build Hybrid Cloud the Right Way with Christoffer Klarskov Jakobsen [MVP]" places it within hybrid cloud design. Related episodes include "Azure Update Manager - Simply Explained", "Azure Resource Manager - Simply Explained" and "Secure Azure Automation with Ahmed Uzejnovic [MVP]".

azure-artifacts.desc: Azure Artifacts is the Azure DevOps package management service for hosting private NuGet, npm, Maven, Python and Universal package feeds, with support for upstream sources.

faq.a: Azure Artifacts is the package management service in Azure DevOps. It hosts private feeds for NuGet, npm, Maven, Python and Universal packages.
faq.q: What is Azure Artifacts?

faq.a: It supports NuGet, npm, Maven, Python and Universal packages.
faq.q: Which package types does Azure Artifacts support?

faq.a: Yes. Feeds in Azure Artifacts can proxy public upstream sources, so public packages can be accessed through the same feed as private ones.
faq.q: Can Azure Artifacts use public package sources?

azure-artifacts.long:
Azure Artifacts is the package management service within Azure DevOps. It hosts private feeds for several package types: NuGet, npm, Maven, Python and Universal packages. Teams use it to publish and consume the packages their own code produces, and to keep those packages in a controlled location instead of distributing them informally.

A feed in Azure Artifacts can also proxy public upstream sources. This means that packages from public registries can be reached through the same feed that holds a team's private packages, giving developers a single source to configure in their build and development tools.

Azure Artifacts is one of the services that make up Azure DevOps, alongside the other components used to plan, build and release software. It is typically referenced when discussing how dependencies and build outputs are stored and shared in a delivery pipeline.

On M365.FM, Azure Artifacts appears in the context of Azure DevOps topics. The episode "Azure DevOps - Simply Explained" covers Azure DevOps as a whole, and "GitHub vs Azure DevOps for Microsoft Fabric CI/CD" looks at how Azure DevOps compares with GitHub for continuous integration and delivery with Microsoft Fabric. Official documentation for getting started with the service is available on Microsoft Learn.

azure-automation.desc: Azure Automation is a Microsoft cloud service for process automation with runbooks, configuration management and update management across Azure and on-premises environments.

faq.a: Azure Automation is a cloud-based automation service from Microsoft that supports process automation with runbooks, configuration management and update management. It works across Azure and on-premises environments.
faq.q: What is Azure Automation?

faq.a: Azure Automation is part of Microsoft Azure and is developed by Microsoft.
faq.q: Which Microsoft platform is Azure Automation part of?

faq.a: Episodes include "Azure Automation - Simply Explained", "Secure Azure Automation with Ahmed Uzejnovic [MVP]", "Automate Intune Device Cleanup with Azure Automation" and "PowerShell Automation for Azure and Microsoft 365 with Matthew Dowst [MVP]".
faq.q: Which M365.FM episodes cover Azure Automation?

azure-automation.long:
Azure Automation is a cloud-based automation service developed by Microsoft and part of Microsoft Azure. It is categorized as a Microsoft tool and is used for process automation with runbooks, configuration management and update management. Its scope covers resources in Azure as well as on-premises environments.

Typical uses of the service include scripting recurring operational tasks as runbooks, managing configuration, and handling updates for machines across hybrid setups. Official product documentation is published by Microsoft on Microsoft Learn.

On M365.FM, Azure Automation appears in several episodes. "Azure Automation - Simply Explained" covers the service as an introduction. "Secure Azure Automation with Ahmed Uzejnovic [MVP]" addresses securing automation workloads, and "PowerShell Automation for Azure and Microsoft 365 with Matthew Dowst [MVP]" looks at PowerShell-based automation across Azure and Microsoft 365. Practical scenarios are discussed in "Automate Intune Device Cleanup with Azure Automation" and "Build an Automated Azure Cleanup Engine to Reduce Cloud Waste". A related episode, "Build Enterprise Automation with Azure Logic Apps", covers another Azure automation service.

azure-automation-state-configuration.desc: Azure Automation State Configuration is a PowerShell Desired State Configuration (DSC) based service that keeps machines in a defined state and reports compliance.

faq.a: It is a configuration management service based on PowerShell Desired State Configuration (DSC). It keeps machines in a defined desired state and reports their compliance.
faq.q: What is Azure Automation State Configuration?

faq.a: Microsoft is moving this capability to Azure Machine Configuration. The Microsoft Learn documentation should be checked for current details on the transition.
faq.q: Is Azure Automation State Configuration being replaced?

faq.a: It is based on PowerShell Desired State Configuration (DSC), which describes the intended configuration of a machine and enforces it.
faq.q: What technology is Azure Automation State Configuration based on?

azure-automation-state-configuration.long:
Azure Automation State Configuration is a configuration management service built on PowerShell Desired State Configuration (DSC). It is used to define how machines should be configured and to keep them in that defined desired state over time.

Beyond applying configurations, the service reports on compliance, showing whether managed machines match the state that was declared for them. This makes it relevant for administrators who want a consistent, auditable configuration baseline across their systems.

Microsoft is moving this capability to Azure Machine Configuration. Anyone evaluating or maintaining solutions built on Azure Automation State Configuration should therefore review the current Microsoft documentation for the latest guidance on the transition.

No episodes on M365.FM currently reference Azure Automation State Configuration, and no related topics are linked to this entry at present. Official details are available in the Microsoft Learn documentation for the Azure Automation DSC overview.

azure-backup.desc: Azure Backup is Microsoft's managed cloud backup service for Azure VMs, databases, file shares, blobs, disks and on-premises servers, with policy-based retention in a vault.

faq.a: Azure Backup is Microsoft's managed cloud backup service. It stores recovery points in a vault and applies policy-based retention to the protected data.
faq.q: What is Azure Backup?

faq.a: It protects Azure VMs, databases, file shares, blobs, disks and on-premises servers.
faq.q: What can Azure Backup protect?

faq.a: It is the subject of "Azure Backup - Simply Explained" and "Harden Azure Backup with Soft Delete, MUA, and Vault Lock", and it relates to other episodes on cloud security, Microsoft 365 backup, Azure Site Recovery and Azure Files.
faq.q: Where is Azure Backup discussed on M365.FM?

azure-backup.long:
Azure Backup is Microsoft's managed cloud backup service. It protects a range of workloads, including Azure virtual machines, databases, file shares, blobs, disks and on-premises servers. Backup data is stored as recovery points in a vault, and retention is controlled through policies.

The service is used to keep restorable copies of data so that workloads can be recovered after accidental deletion, corruption or other loss. Because retention is policy-based, administrators define how long recovery points are kept rather than managing individual backup copies by hand.

On M365.FM, Azure Backup is covered in several episodes. "Azure Backup - Simply Explained" introduces the service. "Harden Azure Backup with Soft Delete, MUA, and Vault Lock" looks at protective controls for backup vaults. Related topics appear in "Hidden Microsoft 365 and Azure Cloud Security Risks", "Microsoft 365 Backup with Isolated Vault Architecture", and the companion explainers "Azure Site Recovery - Simply Explained" and "Azure Files - Simply Explained", which address disaster recovery and file share storage in the same ecosystem.

azure-bastion.desc: Azure Bastion is a managed Microsoft Azure service that provides secure RDP and SSH access to virtual machines through the Azure portal, without public IP addresses.

faq.a: Azure Bastion is a managed Microsoft Azure service that provides secure RDP and SSH access to virtual machines through the Azure portal, without requiring public IP addresses on those machines.
faq.q: What is Azure Bastion?

faq.a: Azure Bastion is developed by Microsoft and is part of Microsoft Azure.
faq.q: Who develops Azure Bastion?

faq.a: The episode "Azure Bastion - Simply Explained" covers it directly. It is also relevant to "Azure Virtual Network - Simply Explained", "Azure Firewall - Simply Explained" and "Secure Azure Networking with Rex de Koning [MVP-MCT]".
faq.q: Which M365.FM episodes cover Azure Bastion?

azure-bastion.long:
Azure Bastion is a managed service from Microsoft that is part of Microsoft Azure. It provides secure Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) and Secure Shell (SSH) access to virtual machines through the Azure portal, so the virtual machines do not need to be exposed through public IP addresses.

The service is used when administrators need to reach virtual machines for management or troubleshooting while keeping those machines off the public internet. Instead of opening RDP or SSH ports directly to external networks, access is brokered by the managed Azure Bastion service. M365.FM classifies it as both a Microsoft tool and an identity and security tool, reflecting its role in reducing the exposed attack surface of virtual infrastructure.

Azure Bastion is closely related to other Azure networking topics, such as Azure Virtual Network and Azure Firewall, which together form part of how access and traffic are controlled in Azure environments. Official documentation is published on Microsoft Learn.

On M365.FM, Azure Bastion is covered in the episode "Azure Bastion - Simply Explained". It also comes up in related networking episodes, including "Azure Virtual Network - Simply Explained", "Azure Firewall - Simply Explained" and "Secure Azure Networking with Rex de Koning [MVP-MCT]".

azure-blob-storage.desc: Azure Blob Storage is Microsoft's object storage service for unstructured data, with hot, cool, cold and archive access tiers that trade lower storage cost for higher access cost.

faq.a: Azure Blob Storage is Microsoft's object storage service for unstructured data. It organizes stored data into hot, cool, cold and archive access tiers.
faq.q: What is Azure Blob Storage?

faq.a: The tiers trade storage cost against access cost. Cooler tiers charge less for storage but more for access, and the archive tier also introduces rehydration delays before data can be read.
faq.q: What is the difference between the Azure Blob Storage access tiers?

faq.a: It is the subject of the episode "Azure Blob Storage - Simply Explained" and is also discussed in "Archive Inactive SharePoint Sites with Azure Blob Storage". It is covered alongside storage accounts, disk storage and Event Grid in other episodes.
faq.q: Where does Azure Blob Storage appear on M365.FM?

azure-blob-storage.long:
Azure Blob Storage is Microsoft's object storage service for unstructured data. It is used to store data that does not fit a relational or file-based structure, and it organizes that data into access tiers so storage can be matched to how often the data is read.

The service offers four access tiers: hot, cool, cold and archive. Moving data to a cooler tier lowers the storage charges, but it comes with higher access costs or, in the case of the archive tier, delays when data has to be rehydrated before it can be used again. Choosing a tier is therefore a trade-off between ongoing storage cost and the cost and time of retrieving the data. Microsoft documents these tiers in its access tiers overview on Microsoft Learn.

On M365.FM, Azure Blob Storage appears in several episodes. The episode "Azure Blob Storage - Simply Explained" covers the service directly. "Archive Inactive SharePoint Sites with Azure Blob Storage" looks at using it for archiving. Related Azure topics are covered in "Azure Storage Accounts - Simply Explained", "Azure Disk Storage - Simply Explained" and "Event Grid - Simply Explained", and the service is also placed within the learning path in "7 Levels of Azure Administration: Beginner to Cloud Architect".

azure-boards.desc: Azure Boards is the Azure DevOps service for planning and tracking work using work items, backlogs, sprints, queries, dashboards and Kanban boards.

faq.a: Azure Boards is the Azure DevOps service for planning and tracking work. It uses work items, backlogs, sprints, queries, dashboards and Kanban boards.
faq.q: What is Azure Boards?

faq.a: It is used to plan, organize and track work. Backlogs and sprints support planning, Kanban boards visualize progress, and queries and dashboards help review work item status.
faq.q: What can Azure Boards be used for?

faq.a: It is relevant to the episodes "Azure DevOps - Simply Explained", "GitHub vs Azure DevOps for Microsoft Fabric CI/CD" and "Monitor Compliance in Microsoft Defender for Cloud".
faq.q: Where does Azure Boards appear on M365.FM?

azure-boards.long:
Azure Boards is a service within Azure DevOps used to plan and track work. It organizes work through work items and provides several ways to view and manage them, including backlogs, sprints, queries, dashboards and Kanban boards.

Teams use Azure Boards to capture tasks and track their progress. Backlogs and sprints support planning over time, while Kanban boards give a visual view of work as it moves through stages. Queries and dashboards help filter work items and summarize their status. Because Azure Boards is one service in the broader Azure DevOps offering, it sits alongside the other tools in that suite.

On M365.FM, Azure Boards is relevant to the episode "Azure DevOps - Simply Explained", which covers Azure DevOps as a whole. It also appears in the context of "GitHub vs Azure DevOps for Microsoft Fabric CI/CD", which compares the two platforms, and "Monitor Compliance in Microsoft Defender for Cloud".

Microsoft documents the service in its Azure DevOps documentation on Microsoft Learn, in an overview titled "What is Azure Boards".
